 "Have Korea Make Our Shampoo," Walmart Comes Calling... Korean Shampoo a Hit in U.S., Exports Surge 83%
 by Kwon Jaehee 
 Published 17 Nov.2026 08:58(KST) 
 Updated 17 Nov.2026 13:31(KST) 
 open/close 
 Share 
 Language 
 Text Size 
 Print 
 Walmart Purchasing Team to Visit Korea on November 18
KOTRA to Hold Private-Label Sourcing Consultation
K-Beauty Expands Beyond Skincare into Haircare
 View original image 
 Walmart, the largest retailer in the United States, is seeking Korean manufacturers to produce private-label (PB) cosmetics. As K-beauty’s popularity expands from skincare to haircare—with U.S. exports of Korean shampoo surging more than 80%—major local retailers are beginning to take an interest in Korean companies’ manufacturing capabilities. Attention is focused on whether South Korea’s cosmetics industry will expand its presence in the U.S. beyond exports of its own brands and become part of global retailers’ PB supply chains.
 According to industry sources on November 17, the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) will hold a Walmart PB sourcing consultation event at its headquarters in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on November 18. The event was organized to explore potential partnerships between Walmart’s purchasing team, which is visiting South Korea, and local beauty and personal care manufacturers. KOTRA accepted applications from around five Korean manufacturers from November 4 to 11.
 View original image 
 Walmart is interested in haircare, body care, and lotion products. Eligible participants are companies capable of supplying PB products to the U.S. market or providing products through original equipment manufacturing (OEM) or original design manufacturing (ODM). Applicants were required to have company and product materials in English and products registered with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA).
 According to Korea Customs Service trade statistics, South Korea’s shampoo exports totaled $179.57 million from January through September 2026, up 39% from the same period last year. In just nine months, exports had already surpassed the full-year total of $178.07 million in 2025. Growth in the U.S. market was particularly pronounced. During the same period, exports of Korean shampoo to the United States surged 83.1% year over year to $40.85 million. The United States overtook China to become the largest market for Korean shampoo. K-beauty exports, which have grown primarily on the strength of skincare, are expanding to include scalp and haircare products.
 Growth in the U.S. haircare market is also evident. According to market research firm Circana, haircare sales through U.S. premium retail channels rose 11% year over year in the first half of 2026. Hair serum sales increased by about 60%.
 View original image 
 The haircare market is growing in part because consumer trends are shifting toward caring for the scalp and hair like skin. Once centered on shampoo and conditioner, the market has recently expanded into specialized care, with consumers using serums, tonics, and essences based on scalp conditions and hair concerns. Demand for premium products is also rising as the “Skinification” trend spreads, encouraging consumers to choose functional products for their scalp and hair just as they select cosmetics suited to their facial skin. This shift in consumer behavior is creating new market opportunities for K-beauty companies that have primarily grown through skincare.
 “Skinification, the trend of caring for the scalp and hair like skin, has recently been gaining traction around the world,” said Jung Jiyoon, an analyst at NH Investment & Securities. “Haircare products account for just 4% of cosmetics exports, making them a category with significant growth potential. In 2027, growth in haircare exports is expected to outpace the overall export growth rate.”
 Korean beauty companies are also stepping up efforts to expand their haircare businesses with a focus on the U.S. market. Amorepacific is targeting North America with brands including Mise-en-scène, Ryo, and Laboh. It is expanding its product range, including scalp essences and hair oils, to cater to the diverse hair types and care routines of local consumers. Amorepacific has set a goal of generating KRW 1 trillion in haircare sales and achieving an overseas sales share of at least 60% in the fiscal year running from July 2029 to June 2030.
 LG Household & Health Care is also expanding its sales network in the U.S. market through its haircare brand Dr. Groot. One distinctive feature is its dedicated product range for North American consumers, which is not sold in South Korea. The range includes shampoo, treatments, and scalp serums. In August 2026, the brand entered 424 Sephora stores across the United States.

 It remains uncertain whether the consultation event will lead to actual supply contracts. Details such as Walmart’s order volumes, supply prices, and supplier selection have not been disclosed. “We are unable to disclose the names of the Korean cosmetics manufacturers participating in the event, in consideration of requests from the companies,” a KOTRA official said. “The event is intended to explore the possibility of future cooperation on PB product supply.”
